content: The recommended intravenous dosage is 500-1000 mL (30-60 g), not exceeding 1500 mL per day (20 mL/kg). It is essential to monitor the patient’s complete blood count (CBC) with differential, hemoglobin (Hgb), hematocrit (Hct), prothrombin time (PT), and partial thromboplastin time (PTT). For patients with a creatinine clearance (CrCl) of less than 10 mL/min, after administering the initial dose, subsequent doses should be reduced by 20-50% of the normal dose. The recommended dose is 10 mL/kg per administration, with a maximum limit of 20 mL/kg. When using Hespan (250-700 mL), which contains added citrate anticoagulant, it should be mixed at a ratio of 1:8 to 1:13 with venous whole blood. This product should not be administered with blood through the same intravenous (IV) administration set. IV tubing should be changed or flushed thoroughly with normal saline (NS) before administering blood through the same line. Additionally, IV tubing must be replaced at least every 24 hours. Anaphylactoid reactions are possible, so epinephrine and resuscitative equipment should be readily available during administration. In animal studies involving New Zealand rabbits, BD rats, and Swiss mice, no evidence of teratogenicity was observed when the product was administered at doses equivalent to two times, one-third times, and one time the maximum recommended therapeutic human dose, respectively, during gestation. However, it is unknown whether this product is excreted in human breast milk. Since many drugs are excreted in breast milk, caution is advised when administering this product to nursing women. The product is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. The infusion rate should not exceed 2 g/kg/hour (20 mL/kg/hour). The product should be stored at room temperature and must not be frozen. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. Medications should not be flushed down the toilet or poured into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for every individual. It is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. For side effects, U.S. residents should contact their doctor, while Canadian residents should also consult their healthcare provider. This information was last revised in May 2024.
